q: Nutritional rickets is characterised by all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Phosphate is low in nutritional rickets; a raised phosphate points to chronic kidney disease.

q: A 4-month-old infant has vitamin D deficiency rickets. Which sign are you most likely to find?
e: Craniotabes is the early sign in young infants; bow legs appear only after walking, and the fontanelle is large.

q: All of the following are signs of rickets EXCEPT:
o: Thickening of the wrists and ankles
e: Conjunctivitis is not a feature of rickets.

q: The most common cause of rickets is:
e: Nutritional rickets (vitamin D and/or calcium deficiency) is by far the commonest.

q: A breastfed infant has nutritional rickets with low calcium and raised alkaline phosphatase. Which hormone is raised?
e: Low calcium absorption causes secondary hyperparathyroidism.

q: The best blood marker to follow the activity and healing of rickets is:
e: ALP rises early with active rickets and falls to normal with healing.

q: Clinical features of rickets include all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Rickets gives hypotonia, delay, bossing and wide wrists; obesity is not a feature.

q: A 2-year-old has bow legs, wide wrists, low phosphate, high ALP and low 25(OH)D. Best treatment?
o: Vitamin D 3000–6000 IU daily for 12 weeks plus calcium
e: Nutritional rickets: treatment-dose vitamin D for 12 weeks with calcium 500 mg/day, then maintenance.

q: Rickets with alopecia and a very high serum 1,25(OH)2D is most likely:
e: Type 2 is end-organ (receptor) resistance: 1,25(OH)2D is high and alopecia is typical.

q: A boy has bow legs after walking, very low phosphate, normal calcium and normal PTH; his mother is short with bowed legs. Diagnosis?
e: Renal phosphate loss with normal PTH, inherited X-linked dominant.

q: The earliest X-ray sign of healing rickets after vitamin D is:
o: A dense white calcification line at the metaphysis
e: A line of provisional calcification appears within 2–4 weeks.

q: The recommended vitamin D supplement to prevent rickets in infancy is:
o: 400 IU daily from birth to 12 months
e: 400 IU daily for every infant from birth to 12 months, however fed.
k: vitamin d 400 iu daily from birth to 12 months

q: An infant with rickets has a seizure; serum calcium is 1.5 mmol/L. Best immediate treatment?
o: 10% calcium gluconate 0.5 ml/kg IV over 10 minutes
e: Correct symptomatic hypocalcaemia with IV calcium under monitoring, then oral calcium and vitamin D.

q: Which statement about the rosary of rickets is correct?
o: It is a rounded, painless swelling of the costochondral junctions
It is due to subperiosteal bleeding
It is at the sternoclavicular joint
e: The scorbutic rosary is sharp and tender; the rachitic rosary is rounded and painless.
